chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUthmān, from Samāʿah, who said:
I asked him about the urine of a boy that comes onto a garment, and he said: “Wash it.” I said: “What if I do not find its place?” He said: “Wash the entire garment.”

key_terms.اغْسِلْهُ: wash it; the command to cleanse the affected area
key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment or clothing affected by impurity
key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: a boy or young child whose urine is being discussed
key_terms.بَوْلِ: urine; the substance causing najasah in this ruling
key_terms.كُلَّهُ: all of it; indicating the entire garment must be washed if the spot is unknown
key_terms.مَكَانَهُ: its place; the specific location of the impurity on the garment

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a child’s urine gets on a garment and its exact place is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the najasah of a garment affected by the urine of a boy. It instructs that the affected place should be washed, and if the exact location is unknown, the entire garment should be washed to ensure taharah.
